text:
jenny_acme: hitting a repeatable failure with JSON mode + pydantic validation — model returns invalid JSON (trailing comma + escaped newlines) and my SDK raises JSONDecodeError. started after a model update this morning.

jenny_acme: here's the snippet from the streaming response we get just before the parse error:
```
{"task": "summarize", "result": "Line1\\nLine2",}
```

jenny_acme: curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"...","jsonmode":"structured","schema_id":"acme-order-v2"}'
```

sam_support: sorry about that — can you paste the exact error you see from pydantic?

jenny_acme: stack: 
```
pydantic.errors.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)
During validation, caught exception while decoding JSON
```

eli_support: do you get this only when streaming or also with non-streaming responses?

jenny_acme: only streaming. non-streaming returns valid JSON occasionally, but streaming often cuts chunks and yields trailing commas in the reconstructed payload.

anya_eng_ml: this sounds like a stream-reassembly edge — the runtime may be flushing chunk boundaries that end with a "," or with an escaped newline that the client merges incorrectly. can you share the exact raw chunks (if you have them)?

jenny_acme: attaching raw chunks (copied):
```
{"task": "summarize", "result": "Line1\\nLi\n{\"ne2\",}
```

sam_support: thanks. reproducing locally now. i'm seeing the same fragments. when we join chunks naively the concatenation produces trailing commas.

trent_eng_runtime: tagging in eng-runtime. two quick questions: 1) which SDK and version? 2) are you using the client-side stream reassembly or our x-stream-chunk header?

jenny_acme: using python-sdk 0.9.1, built-in stream handler. not modifying reassembly.

anya_eng_ml: also worth noting: we saw schema drift earlier — the schema acme-order-v2 expects an enum for "priority": ["primary","tertiary"], but model sometime returns "secondary" which pydantic complains about after parse. so there's two failure classes: parse errors from streaming + semantic validation errors.

marco_eng_infra: quick check on the API side: I see a couple 401 auth failures right before the stream for this customer (token rotated). could that lead to truncated/broken streams? infra-bot created a ticket if you want trace: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INF-5321

infra-bot: ticket INF-5321 created: "stream reassembly + schema drift causing JSON parse failures for jenny_acme" assigned P2.

eli_support: for an immediate workaround, can you set jsonmode to "relaxed" or use the non-streaming endpoint while we triage? relaxed will attempt to coerce and return raw_text on parse failure.

jenny_acme: relaxed helped reduce crashes but now pydantic raises: 
```
pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Order
priority
  unexpected value; permitted: 'primary', 'tertiary' (type=value_error.const; given='secondary')
```

anya_eng_ml: for enum mismatches we usually do two things: 1) expand schema to include fallback enum labels (short-term), 2) detect unknown enum values and map them to a fallback path (e.g., set priority='unknown' and surface in analytics). i'll open a model-eval to see why the model emits 'secondary' for that prompt.

trent_eng_runtime: on the streaming parse side I can push a runtime patch to sanitize chunk boundaries (strip trailing commas and attempt to rejoin JSON fragments more conservatively). need a failing example and the request ID; can you share request-id from response headers?

jenny_acme: request-id: rwd_79a3f2c4. also saw latency spikes ~800ms around the same timeframe.

sam_support: capturing: request-id rwd_79a3f2c4, customer session id, raw chunks, stack traces. escalating to eng-runtime (trent) and eng-ml (anya).

anya_eng_ml: next steps from ML side: run eval on the prompt set -> measure frequency of enum drift -> classify whether this is model-update induced. if it's a regression we'll rollback the model variant and pin v1.2.3 for accounts using acme-order-v2.

trent_eng_runtime: I created a small patch branch that does two things: a) buffer streaming tokens until we see a full top-level JSON close, b) trim spurious trailing commas before final parse. pushing to canary in 1h for 5% of traffic.

infra-bot: canary deploy started: runtime/sanitize-stream-chunks v2026.03.17-canary -> 5% traffic.

eli_support: FYI this also surfaced with zod clients where zod reported "Expected object, received string" — likely because of reassembly ordering. that confirms runtime chunk issue rather than a single language binding bug.

marco_eng_infra: changed token rotation logging and ensured 401s now return an explicit error body rather than partial stream. will monitor.

anya_eng_ml: created model-eval job: MEVAL-2247 to track enum drift on acme prompts. assigning to @anya_eng_ml.

trent_eng_runtime: patch pushed to canary. sam/eli — can you ask jenny to test again with streaming on canary by adding header X-Runtime-Canary: sanitize-1 ?

sam_support: @jenny_acme, could you re-run with that header and paste results?

jenny_acme: re-ran with header. streaming now returns full JSON in our reassembly and pydantic parses successfully for majority of cases. still seeing ~0.5% of messages with unknown enum values.

anya_eng_ml: good — i'll handle the enum fallback and add a schema compatibility shim in our schema-service so unknown enums map to 'unknown' before pydantic validation. will roll patch today.

sam_support: leaving this thread open until INF-5321 is resolved and CANARY passes to 100%. tagging P2 -> assign to trent & anya. :eyes:

jenny_acme: thanks team — workaround worked and the customer is unblocked for now. appreciate the quick triage.

trent_eng_runtime: marking follow-ups: 1) promote sanitize-stream-chunks to 100% after 24h canary, 2) add integration test for chunked JSON with trailing commas, 3) ensure our SDKs expose a tolerant reassembly mode.

infra-bot: INF-5321 updated: canary healthy at 5%, monitoring.

sam_support: closing loop later today once canary reaches 100%.

jenny_acme: :heart:
